Trump-Putin Diesel Deal Sparks International Concern and Bipartisan Opposition

Russian diesel exports have resumed to global markets following an agreement involving US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The Kremlin stated these supplies could help stabilize oil markets, though they may not be sufficient. The deal has drawn criticism, with bipartisan senators demanding Trump scrap it, calling it a 'betrayal' of US allies. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev, however, broke ranks with EU leaders to back the agreement, welcoming the controversial deal.
